name: Fabrizio Sergi
title: Associate Professor of Biomedical and Mechanical Engineering
department: Biomedical Engineering and Mechanical Engineering; Human Robotics (HuRo) Lab
fitReason: Strong assistive-robotics AI match for Gaussian-process modeling, online optimization and human-robot adaptation. The recent work learns time-varying human input-output relationships and changes an actual exoskeleton control parameter, rather than merely studying human motor learning or collecting clinical data.

physicalEvidence.summary: Full January 2026 accepted RA-L paper validates dynamic Bayesian optimization against standard BO on a real Active Pelvis Orthosis hip exoskeleton with 16 healthy participants at Delaware. The Gaussian-process covariance includes time to discount older observations; the learned optimizer iteratively updates one hip-torque amplitude parameter through Simulink, while gait phase and low-level execution remain classical. Participants complete two approximately 15-minute sessions, with an unannounced-to-the-optimizer treadmill-speed increase inducing non-stationarity. DBO performs better in later validation stages, but both methods have residual error and no significant difference in secondary propulsion outcomes. This is single-parameter laboratory training with healthy adults, not demonstrated clinical efficacy after stroke, generalized whole-body control, or an autonomous outdoor wearable policy. First author GilHwan Kim is independently verified as Sergi’s lab doctoral graduate in April 2026.
